<parameter name="content"># Docs restructuring plan

Principle: every fact has exactly one home. Every other place either links to that home or says nothing.

## 1. Local setup steps (duplicated and drifted)

| Copy | Content | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| README.md | clone, `npm install`, copy `.env.example`, `npm run dev` | **Canonical.** Keep this under a `## Local setup` heading. |
| CONTRIBUTING.md | clone, `npm ci`, create `.env` by hand, `npm start` | **Delete the steps.** Replace them with one line: "Set up your environment by following [Local setup](README.md#local-setup)." |

Why README wins:
- `npm run dev` is the current command. The project's own history says the team switched from `npm start` to `npm run dev` after a port clash, so CONTRIBUTING's `npm start` is stale.
- Copying `.env.example` is reproducible. Creating `.env` by hand is not.

Setup belongs in README because anyone running the tool needs it, not only contributors.

Before merging:
- Confirm `package.json` still defines a `dev` script.
- Decide whether to adopt `npm ci` (the one possibly-better detail in CONTRIBUTING's copy) in the README steps. If adopted, it goes in README only.

## 2. API request timeout (contradictory: 30s vs 45s)

| Copy | Decision |
|---|---|
| `src/http/client.js` (the timeout constant) | **Canonical.** The code is the source of truth. |
| README.md ("time out after 30 seconds") | **Remove the number.** Replace with: "API requests time out after a fixed limit. See the timeout constant in `src/http/client.js`." |
| CONTRIBUTING.md ("time out after 45 seconds") | **Delete the sentence entirely.** Contributors can read the code, and README already points there. |

At least one of these docs is wrong today, and both will go stale on the next change. So no prose doc should restate the value.

When making this edit:
- Check the actual constant.
- If anyone relied on the documented number, note which doc was wrong in the PR description, not in the docs.

## 3. Support email (not duplicated)

| Copy | Decision |
|---|---|
| README.md | **Canonical. Keep as is.** No other copies exist, and none should be added. CONTRIBUTING can link to README if it needs to. |

## 4. Billing rule: "always call `recalcTotals()` after any mutation to line items" (misplaced)

| Copy | Decision |
|---|---|
| Draft CLAUDE.md | **Remove.** CLAUDE.md is loaded for every task. This rule only matters in one file, so it is noise everywhere else. |
| `src/billing.js` | **Canonical.** Add a short comment at the line-item mutation code (or at the top of the module) stating the invariant. Anyone editing that file, human or agent, will see it exactly when it applies. |

Preferred follow-up: enforce the invariant in code so the comment becomes unnecessary. Either have the line-item mutators call `recalcTotals()` themselves, or route all mutations through one helper that does. If that is done, delete the comment.

## 5. "Lessons learned" section in draft CLAUDE.md (misplaced history)

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| "2025-11: switched from `npm start` to `npm run dev` after port clash" | **Delete.** The current fact (use `npm run dev`) already lives in README's setup steps (item 1). The story behind it belongs in git history and the original PR. |
| "2026-01: renamed the export module..." | **Delete.** The rename is recorded in git history, and the code shows the current name. |
| The section as a whole | **Delete.** Narrated history is not an instruction. It costs context on every task and invites agents to act on outdated states. If the team wants a human-readable record, put it in a `CHANGELOG.md`, not CLAUDE.md. |

If any lesson encodes a rule that still applies and isn't obvious from the code, keep only the rule. Put it in present tense, in the narrowest place it applies: a code comment if it's file-specific, CLAUDE.md only if it's genuinely repo-wide.

## 6. Resulting CLAUDE.md

After items 4 and 5, the draft CLAUDE.md has no content left. **Do not create it** until there is a genuinely repo-wide instruction an agent couldn't infer from the code (for example, "run `npm test` before committing"). Setup steps should not be copied into it either; at most it can link to README's Local setup.

## Summary of edits

- **README.md:** keep the setup steps (canonical), add a `## Local setup` anchor, replace the "30 seconds" sentence with a pointer to `src/http/client.js`, keep the support email.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md:** delete the setup steps and replace them with a link to README#local-setup; delete the "45 seconds" sentence.
- **src/billing.js:** add the `recalcTotals()` invariant comment, or better, enforce it in code.
- **src/http/client.js:** unchanged. It remains the single source for the timeout.
- **CLAUDE.md (draft):** remove the billing rule and the entire Lessons learned section, and don't ship the now-empty file.
</parameter>
</invoke>
**docs-plan.md is written.** The source files aren't in this directory, so I couldn't check the real timeout value or `package.json`. The plan lists both as checks to do before merging.

| Fact | Single home | Every other copy |
|---|---|---|
| Setup steps | `README.md` (`npm run dev`, copy `.env.example`) | `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s drifted copy is deleted and replaced with a link to README. |
| API timeout | The constant in `src/http/client.js` | Both "30s" (README) and "45s" (CONTRIBUTING) are removed. README just points to the code, and CONTRIBUTING says nothing. |
| Support email | `README.md` | It has no duplicates and stays as is. |
| `recalcTotals()` rule | A comment in `src/billing.js` | It's removed from CLAUDE.md. Better still, enforce the rule in code and drop the comment too. |
| Lessons learned | Git history (or a CHANGELOG if wanted) | The whole section is deleted from CLAUDE.md. The one live fact in it, `npm run dev`, is already covered by README's setup steps. |
| CLAUDE.md itself | — | Nothing is left in it, so don't ship it until there's a real repo-wide instruction. |

**Why README's setup steps win:** the lessons-learned section says the team switched from `npm start` to `npm run dev`, so CONTRIBUTING's `npm start` is out of date.

**Open question:** the team should decide whether to adopt CONTRIBUTING's `npm ci` in the canonical README steps.
